title: Scenario Kernel Language Projection Profile
description: Declares how one language's structural projector turns canonical kernel schemas into language-native source. Governs the DATA a projector consumes, not the projector's own mechanical schema-walking logic (that is shared across languages and does not vary). Every field here was reverse-derived from, and cross-checked against, an already-admitted hand-written embodiment before being formalized — this schema records real, verified policy, not aspirational design.

language.description: Open target identity resolved through language-target-registration.v1.

typeStrategy.description: Free-text label for the language construct emitted per canonical object, e.g. 'record', 'interface', 'frozen-dataclass'. Documentation, not machine-branched — the renderer's own emission function is what actually decides this, one per language.

memberNaming.description: How a schema's camelCase property name becomes a member identifier.

arrayStrategy.description: Free-text label for how an array schema is rendered, e.g. 'ireadonlylist', 'array', 'tuple'.

openPayloadType.description: The type emitted for a fully open ({}) schema — e.g. 'object?', 'unknown', 'object'. Required-ness and nullability are independent for this type in every language observed so far, because JSON Schema's {} permits null as a value regardless of whether the key itself is required; each language's renderer applies its own type system's rule for expressing that, which is why this is a single string here rather than a nullable/non-nullable pair — the nullability handling itself is intrinsic to the language, not a policy choice this profile makes.

defaultStrategy.description: What an optional property with a schema-declared `default` becomes. 'materialize-in-model': bake the schema default in as the language's own default value, with a non-nullable type (C#'s verified choice: `bool Terminal = false`). 'preserve-optional': ignore the schema default for modeling purposes, always emit a nullable/optional member with no baked value, pushing the default to call sites (Node's and Python's verified choice, both with an explicit comment explaining why: `terminal?: boolean` / `terminal: bool | None = None`). This is a genuine per-language policy split, not a universal rule — verified 2-vs-1 across the three admitted embodiments, not assumed.

closedVocabularyStrategy.description: Free-text label for the default treatment of a closed (enum) string schema when no nestedTypeOverrides/enumTypeOverrides entry applies, e.g. 'string' (C#: every enum stays a plain string) or 'string-literal-union'/'typing.Literal' (Node/Python: MOST enums get a named type, via enumTypeOverrides below, but this is the fallback for ones that don't).

nestedTypeOverrides.description: Explicit type names for local/inline schema shapes whose name is not mechanically derivable from parent+field — e.g. gherkin-binding.schema.json's local $defs/step (-> GherkinStep, not GherkinBindingStep) and capability.schema.json's scenarios reference-or-inline-stub union (-> ScenarioReference). Keyed by '<schemaFile>#<jsonPointer>'.

enumTypeOverrides.description: Explicit named-type promotion for specific closed-enum properties, keyed by '<schemaFile>#<jsonPointer>'. A property with no entry here falls back to closedVocabularyStrategy's plain treatment — this is how a language whose default is 'hoist to named type' can still leave a specific property (e.g. language-binding.json's open-ended `implements`) as a plain string, verified as a real exception in both Node and Python rather than assumed uniform.

namespace.description: C#-specific: the namespace generated types are emitted into, distinct from the hand-written namespace to avoid collision within the same implicitly-globbed project.

reservedWordSuffix.description: Python-specific: appended to a member name that collides with a language keyword after naming conversion (e.g. 'from' -> 'from_').

reservedWords.description: Python-specific: the keyword set checked against a converted member name before applying reservedWordSuffix.

constNaming.description: Free-text note on how a schema `const` property is named and where it is placed (e.g. C#: PascalCase static member inside the record body; Node/Python: SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE hoisted to module scope, since interfaces/dataclasses cannot hold a value shared across all instances the way a C# record body can).

optionalFieldStrategy.description: Free-text note on how non-required, non-defaulted properties are rendered (nullable-with-null-default, `?:`, `| None = None`, etc.) — the mechanical half of optionality; defaultStrategy above is the policy half (what happens when the schema also declares a default).

nestedInlineObjectNaming.description: Free-text note on the default (override-less) naming rule for an inline nested object, e.g. '<ParentTypePascalCase><FieldPascalCase>'.

nullViaOneOf.description: Free-text note on how a oneOf[X, {type:'null'}] branch is rendered — independent of whether the property itself is required/optional.

referenceOrInlineStubFlattening.description: Free-text note describing the reference-or-inline-stub union pattern (oneOf[$ref, inline single-identifier-property object]) and that its result type name is never mechanically derivable, always requiring a nestedTypeOverrides entry.

nativeTypePolicy.description: Optional data-driven native type policy used by targets whose type system is not one of the transitional built-in projections.

outputDirectory.description: Path, relative to the language's own directory under languages/, that generated files are written to. Must not overlap with the hand-written source directory.

executionMechanics.description: Language-specific execution embodiment mechanics such as async shape, cancellation, exception identity, construction style, and delegation policy. This section is open-shaped because these mechanics differ in kind by target. Strict-TypeScript target execution providers consume it only after canonical step order, protection kind, and failure disposition have been resolved from scenario-kernel-execution-vector.json into a target-neutral CanonicalExecutionGraph.

schemaRef.description: A kernel/schemas/*.schema.json file, optionally with a '#/$defs/<name>' fragment for a primitive-library definition.
